alignment_bytes.note: Payload sections of envelope binaries start on this boundary.

angle_direction.note: A positive angle turns clockwise on screen (from +x towards +y, y being down).

baked_max_samples.note: A baked track has at most this many samples: frame_step is the smallest integer that keeps it so.

baked_sample_instant.note: Sample i of a baked track is the property's value at the start tick of composition frame first_frame + i * frame_step.

blend_lum_weights.note: Lum() of the Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity blend modes: 0.3 r + 0.59 g + 0.11 b.

color_value_encoding.note: A colour value is [r, g, b, a] in 0..1, straight (not premultiplied) alpha, in the working space's encoding as authored (sRGB-encoded when there is no working space).

compositing_space.note: Layers are composited as premultiplied RGBA, binary32, in the ENCODING of the working space (not linearised) unless the project's `linearize` or `blend_linear` says otherwise (profile document 6.8).

ease_default_influence.note: The influence of a Bezier side that has no stored ease: 1/6. (Profile timeline/1 uses 1/3 for its own, different, ease model.)

ease_default_speed.note: The speed of a Bezier side that has no stored ease: 0.

ease_influence_clamp.note: An ease influence is clamped to this range before use.

endianness.note: Every envelope binary is little-endian. MessagePack header integers inside an envelope are big-endian by MessagePack's own definition (spec/layouts/ENVELOPE.layout.txt section 4).

frame_index_rounding.note: The frame containing tick t is floor(t * num / (254016000000 * den)).

frame_start_rounding.note: Frame f of a rate num/den starts at tick ceil(f * 254016000000 * den / num).

handedness.note: 3D space is left-handed: +x right, +y down, +z INTO the screen (away from the viewer).

hash_algorithm.note: Every files[].sha256, every input_hash, license.sha256, and spec_sha256.

json_binary32.note: A binary32 quantity (a solid's colour, a gradient stop, a text fill) is written as the shortest decimal of the binary64 number equal to it; narrowing what is read to binary32 gives the exact value.

json_integer_width.note: Integers in JSON payloads are exact and may need 64 bits (signed for times, unsigned for ids); a reader must not pass them through binary64.

json_spelling.note: JSON payloads this writer makes are one line: keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, no whitespace, one line feed at the end. Any JSON spelling that satisfies the schemas is valid.

keyframe_extrapolation.note: Before the first keyframe a property has the first keyframe's value, after the last the last's.

keyframe_time.note: Keyframe times are LAYER time: composition time minus the layer's start_time, divided by stretch / 100 (profile document 6.2). The keyframes of a composition's own properties (the global light) are composition time.

layer_order.note: `layers[0]` of a composition is the FRONT (top) layer; layers are composited from the last to the first.

layer_time_rounding.note: Layer time of a stretched layer: (t - start_time) * 100 / stretch computed in binary64 and truncated toward zero to an integer tick. With stretch exactly 100 it is the integer t - start_time.

linear_side_influence.note: A Linear side that meets a Bezier side in one segment acts as an ease along the straight segment with this influence (1/3).

luminance_weights.note: Luminance of a colour for mattes, stencils and effects: 0.2126 r + 0.7152 g + 0.0722 b (binary32).

mask_feather_sigma.note: A Smooth mask feather of f pixels is a Gaussian blur of the coverage with standard deviation f / 2 per axis.

matte_luminance_of.note: A luma matte takes the luminance of the matte layer's PREMULTIPLIED colour.

pixel_origin.note: Pixel coordinates have their origin at the top-left corner of the frame or picture; x grows to the right, y DOWNWARD. The centre of the top-left pixel is (0.5, 0.5).

poster_max_side.note: The longer side of the poster is at most this many pixels.

preview_pixel_format.note: Preview pictures are 8-bit, opaque, in the project's output encoding (sRGB unless the project names another output space), composited over black; row 0 is the top row.

proxy_frame_height.note: Height of a preview proxy frame, pixels.

proxy_max_frames.note: The preview proxy holds at most this many frames.

quantization_levels_16bpc.note: In a 16 bits per channel project: the same with multiples of 1/32768. In a 32 bits per channel project nothing is clamped or rounded.

quantization_levels_8bpc.note: In an 8 bits per channel project: after a layer's source and masks, after each effect, and after each layer is blended, every pixel is clamped (alpha to 0..1, colour to 0..alpha) and each component rounded to a multiple of 1/255, halves up.

range_form.note: A range [start, end) holds start and excludes its end: a layer is active for in_point <= t < out_point, a composition has frames for 0 <= t < duration.

shutter_unit.note: Shutter angle and phase are in degrees of one frame: 360 = one frame duration.

signature_algorithm.note: SIGNATURE.json only. Refusing it is the 'unverified' state, not damage.

spatial_arc_table_cells.note: Arc length along a spatial segment is tabulated at 96 equal parameter steps, each cell integrated by 5-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature (profile document 6.4).

spatial_auto_tangent_divisor.note: An automatic spatial tangent of key i is (value[i+1] - value[i-1]) / 6 (out) and its negative (in); an end key uses itself for the missing neighbour.

stretch_unit.note: A layer's `stretch`: 100 = normal speed, 200 = half speed, negative = reversed.

strip_frame_height.note: Height of a contact strip and of each of its frames, pixels.

strip_frames.note: A contact strip holds this many frames, at times duration * (2 i + 1) / 16 for i = 0..7, left to right.

temporal_ease_model.note: A Bezier side of a key is given by a speed (value units per second) and an influence (fraction of the segment's duration): profile document 6.3.

text_encoding.note: Every text and JSON payload, INCLUDING MANIFEST.json - which is why the scope is container.

text_index_unit.note: Character counts of text runs count Unicode scalar values (code points), not bytes or UTF-16 units.

ticks_per_second.note: Every instant and length is an integer count of ticks; 254 016 000 000 ticks are one second. One frame at num/den fps is 254016000000 * den / num ticks (exact for every broadcast rate).

time_origin.note: Tick 0 is the start of a composition (composition time), the layer's own zero (layer time) or the first frame of a medium (source time). Instants may be negative.

time_remap_unit.note: The value of a layer's `timeRemap` property is source time in seconds (binary64); it is converted to ticks by round(seconds * 254016000000), halves away from zero.

transform_order.note: A layer point p becomes parent-space P = T(position) * O(orientation) * Rz * Ry * Rx * S(scale / 100) * T(-anchor) * p; a 2D layer has only Rz (`rotation`), no orientation, and z scale 1 (profile document 6.7).

note: The machine-readable convention to node-type map of profile motion-comp/1 (SPEC.md section 10.2, ruling S-17). The convention set is a property of the PROFILE, not of the reader (S-25): check these and no others.
